what_it_does: Intel SGX is a trusted execution environment (TEE)—a walled-off secure area on your CPU where sensitive code runs protected from the OS and other software. But SGX applications can still have bugs (stack overflows, logic errors). Finding those bugs is hard because fuzzing (the standard bug-finding technique that throws random inputs at code) can't see inside the secure enclave—it's opaque. IntraFuzz is the first system that fuzzes SGX code from inside the hardware-protected enclave itself, instrumenting code to collect coverage feedback and guide the fuzzing process toward unexplored code paths that might contain vulnerabilities.
